policy: Unavailable real targets are evidence gaps, never skipped passes. Desktop/server artifacts alone do not cover LazyCat, deployed Pages, real Linux host deployment, mobile devices, or native soft keyboards.

gaps.required: Real Chromium acceptance (focus and keyboard navigation, narrow-viewport overflow, touch hit-testing, WebSocket early frames/reconnect, reload restore against a real server) has no automated harness since the demo mode and task acceptance:browser were removed; restore an equivalent harness or record manual evidence before claiming coverage.
Physical iOS/Android layout, coarse pointer, keys bar and native soft-keyboard evidence at 360/560/820px where applicable.
Build and install the Go LazyCat package on a real box; validate manifest injects, upstream image matching and LPK size against the recorded Rust LPK anchors.
Run responsive and WS acceptance against the actual deployed Pages URL; a local Vite build is not deployment evidence.
Install the produced NSIS/DMG on their real target OS versions and document signing/notarization and WebView2/WKWebView runtime results.

Install the server on a real always-on Linux host with a public domain and TLS certificate terminated at a reverse proxy, verify loopback health, browser init/login with a real account, desktop /sync/v2 sign-in and sync, and archive the reverse proxy 401 matrix; local e2e pairs and desktop/server artifacts are not deployment evidence.

Build the LazyCat package with LZC_ARCH=arm64 and run the real-box installation checklist on ARM64 LazyCat hardware, recording architecture-specific evidence; x86_64 box runs and desktop/server builds do not cover it.
